request.spec:
A plan's amount can be changed (an entry and a save button on the plan; PLAN_CHANGED
name=<person> start=<plan start> amount=<new amount>; a bad amount is refused). The new amount
applies to the claims generated from then on; claims already generated keep theirs. Each plan lists
its changes, oldest first, as <date> amount=<amount>.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A plan's amount can be changed (an entry and a save button on the plan; PLAN_CHANGED
name=<person> start=<plan start> amount=<new amount>; a bad amount is refused). The new amount
applies to the claims generated from then on; claims already generated keep theirs. Each plan lists
its changes, oldest first, as <date> amount=<amount>.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I added plan amount changes and the main `plan history` test passes. One of the four tests in the spec, `plan history scenario 1`, still fails, for a reason outside this change (explained below).

**What changed**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V108__plan_change.sql`, adds a `plan_change` table that keeps each change's date and new amount, in the order made.
- **Server:**
  - A new `PlanChange` record is stored with each plan (`Plan.changeAmount(...)`). Changing the amount sets the plan's current amount, so claims generated from then on use it. Claims already generated keep theirs.
  - `PlanService.changeAmount` is new. It refuses an amount below 0.00, and more than two decimals (e.g. `1.005`) is refused by validation. A successful change writes `PLAN_CHANGED sheet=… by=… name=<person> start=<plan start> amount=<new amount>` to the audit file.
  - The new endpoint is `POST /api/sheets/{id}/plans/{planId}/amount`. The existing viewer guard already refuses it for viewers. The plan data sent to the screen now includes its list of changes.
- **Front end:** each plan row now has a `plan-amount` entry and a `plan-amount-save` button. A refusal shows on the row's `plan-error` and is cleared when the entry is edited or saved again. The changes are listed oldest first as `plan-change-line` items reading `<date> amount=<amount>`, where the date is the sheet's today.

**Test results (`bin/e2e`)**
- `plan history`, the test for this change, passes: claim amounts, change lines and audit records all match.
- Scenarios 2 and 3 pass. Scenario 2 crashed once with a browser `SIGSEGV`, then passed on the next two runs.
- Scenario 1 fails every time at line 657. It expects Fay's `person-snapshot-line` to show only `["2026-04-16 0.00"]`, but the app also shows `"2026-03-10 0.00"`.

**Why scenario 1 fails**
Earlier in that test, Ben is merged into Fay. The app's existing merge code deliberately moves the merged person's snapshots across (`carrySnapshots` in `PersonService.java`, which also documents this), so Ben's 03-10 snapshot now shows under Fay. The test expects merges not to carry snapshots. It never touches plan amounts, and this code has nothing to do with plans.

I left the merge behaviour alone because changing how merges work isn't part of this request. To make scenario 1 pass, you would need to decide whether merges should stop carrying snapshots, or carry only some of them; I can make that change if you want.
